newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-MANTILLA ENDS HAAS'S DREAM RUN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MANTILLA ENDS HAAS'S DREAM RUN.

text.p: Spain's Felix Mantilla ended the dream run of unheralded German Tommy Haas on Saturday to book a German Open final berth against Andrei Medvedev.
Haas, a wild card who finished school less than a year ago, looked set to send his third Spanish seed crashing after taking the first set and then romping to 2-0 in the decider.
But Mantilla's experience shone through and he mastered the awkward conditions to win 4-6 6-3 6-4.

Haas, who upset Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya and Alberto Berasategui on his way to the semifinals, was unnerved by two long interruptions for rain and faded during the last three games played in a light drizzle.

"I asked the umpire for the match to be stopped a third time because I thought it was raining a bit too hard and the balls were getting heavy," he said. "This suited Felix because he could get to my shots."
The German, ranked 123 in the world, created good angles by serving from wide in the left court.
But Mantilla, who beat title-holder Roberto Carretero and former Wimbledon champion Boris Becker in earlier rounds, kept cool to outplay his rival from the baseline.
"I think my opponent was a little tired after a very hard week," said 10th-seeded Mantilla. "But he is a young player and I think he can become very good."
Medvedev, ranked 38 in the world, moved to within one match of his third German Open title in four years when he upset second seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov.
Medvedev collected his third seeded scalp of the tournament when he brushed past his Russian opponent 6-3 6-1.

The Ukrainian, who rose to a career-high world ranking of four in 1994, approached the net confidently and unleashed a string of potent passing shots on the rare occasions second-seeded Kafelnikov came to the net.
His victory followed successes over 12th seed Sergei Bruguera and third seed Richard Krajicek.
